newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close higher, outlook seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close higher, outlook seen firm.

text.p: Share prices closed higher in Singapore on Wednesday on a combination of factors that produced an optimism set to continue tomorrow, dealers said.
"I suspect we will see the momentum maintained upwards tomorrow morning," one dealer predicted.
A record high on Wall Street, positive non-oil domestic export figures and a new high on the Hong Kong stock exchange boosted prices in Singapore, dealers agreed.
"The movement was fuelled by Wall Street in the morning, while this afternoon much more attention was paid to the trade figures," one dealer said.
Singapore's Straits Times Industrials Index closed up 24.10 points at 2,194.28 on good volume of 173.77 million shares.
Gainers swamped losers by 254 to 93. Singapore Press, Jurong Shipyard and Rothmans Industries chalked up the best gains.
Dealers said Rothmans buying was probably defensive as the company had a high comparitive yield among blue chips. Rothmans rose 40 cents at S$6.20 on a volume of 1.53 million units.

Ossia International, which made its debut today, was the day's most traded on 29.92 million units. It closed at 68.5 cents after touching a high of 80 cents in early morning trade.-- Nick Edwards, Singapore newsroom (65 8703011)
